indications.description: Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after progression on at least one chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease; prior anthracycline and taxane in the adjuvant or metastatic setting unless unsuitable.
Adults with unresectable liposarcoma after anthracycline-containing treatment for advanced or metastatic disease unless unsuitable.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile (NCCP p2)
Potassium, calcium and magnesium: correct low levels before treatment (EMA SmPC §4.4; NCCP00743 p4)
ECG when heart failure, bradyarrhythmia, QT-prolonging medicines or electrolyte abnormalities are present (NCCP p2)
regular: FBC, renal and liver profile at the start of each cycle (NCCP p2)
FBC before every eribulin dose, including day 8 (EMA SmPC §4.4); confirm treatment-day counts and toxicity before dosing
Periodic potassium, calcium and magnesium; ECG when risk factors or clinical indications require it
Assess neuropathy, infection, mucositis and other toxicity before each dose
monitoring.disease: Scans and other response tests follow the consultant treatment plan. These sources do not mandate a fixed CT, tumour-marker, echo or DXA interval.
monitoring.additional_therapy: If trastuzumab is separately prescribed, add its own cardiac imaging and scheduling plan; this is not routine eribulin-only monitoring.

events: Blood count, kidney and liver tests
Check medicines and potassium/calcium/magnesium; correct low levels
ECG if heart rhythm, cardiac history, medicines or electrolyte risk indicates it
Record baseline neuropathy; plan response scans with the oncology team
Blood count before each dose; kidney/liver profile at cycle start
Review infection symptoms and numbness/tingling before dosing
About 5 minutes for eribulin infusion; allow additional clinic time for tests/preparation

patient_longitudinal_map.phase: Between doses and over later cycles
events: Recovery days at home, without an infusion pump
Periodic electrolytes; repeat ECG if clinically indicated
Scans at the individually agreed response-review interval; no fixed source CT schedule

patient_focus_sparse4: Infection/neutropenia: urgent oncology contact for fever/shivering or feeling suddenly unwell, even between visits
Numbness/tingling or weakness: report early; symptoms may accumulate across cycles
Tiredness/dizziness: pace activities and avoid driving when affected
Heart-rhythm risk: report palpitations, fainting or severe dizziness; ECG/electrolyte checks are tailored to risk
consent_notes: Hair loss, fatigue, peripheral neuropathy and low blood counts/infection are relevant eribulin risks.
Optional trastuzumab combination requires its own regimen, cardiac imaging plan and consent context.

supportive_care.gcsf: May be used for severe neutropenia; no mandatory routine prophylaxis or fixed injection day specified
supportive_care.qt: Review QT-prolonging antiemetics; NCCP00743 p5 explicitly advises considering an ondansetron alternative in predisposed patients.

logistics: Peripheral cannula or existing suitable central line according to access; port not routinely mandated
No home pump, pump connection or pump disconnection in monotherapy
Radiotherapy is not a fixed concurrent component; if required, timeline is agreed separately
source_limitations: Independent consultant and oncology pharmacy validation pending; source reconciliation is not clinical-use authorisation.
Renal/hepatic percentages refer to the original dose; prior reductions and competing pathways require specialist reconciliation.
NCCP cycle-start blood tests supplemented by EMA SmPC FBC before every dose; ECG is risk-triggered, not a universal fixed-cycle schedule.
Current PDF footer states version 8, while its change log records version 9 dated 20/05/2026 for review-schedule amendment only; protocol identity remains nccp-00228-v8.
Table 2 lists CrCl >50 and <50 but leaves exactly 50 mL/min unspecified; equality and legacy ge50 input require review.
